newsitem.title: USA: Reich sees some "give" left in US jobs market - RFTV.
newsitem.headline: Reich sees some "give" left in US jobs market - RFTV.

text.p: Labor Secretary Robert Reich Friday said that despite the strong jobs data for August, there was still some "give" in labor markets.
Interviewed on Reuters Financial Television, Reich said that there was no sign as yet of wage-push inflation despite the strong job creation and reduced unemployment rate.
"Let me assure financial markets, if I may, I still do not see any signs of wages pushing on inflation," he said.
He added that despite the strong picture, the jobs market was not "quite as tight" as the overall picture might suggest.

Reich also said in response to a question as to whether monetary policymakers now needed to "step on the brake," he saw little reason to believe the strong economy was overheating, adding "the economy is percolating, but it is not boiling over."
He added that the drop in the unemployment rate in August to 5.1 percent suggested that the "natural" rate of unemployment may be lower than was assumed a year ago.
